Uzbekistan Blockades Construction Sites Amid Geopolitical Dispute; Major Projects Halted

TASHKENT—Uzbek authorities have blockaded multiple engineering and construction project sites in the Fergana and Navoi regions this week, citing “national security concerns” amid an escalating geopolitical dispute with several foreign contractors. The sudden move has disrupted operations for major firms, including China Petroleum Engineering Corp, and left the future of several large-scale infrastructure projects in question.

As of Thursday, at least eight major construction sites have been sealed off by police and national guard units, according to the Uzbekistan Association of Engineering Contractors. “The authorities arrived without prior notice and ordered an immediate halt to all work pending further instructions,” said Sirojiddin Karimov, representative of the association. “This action has affected thousands of skilled and unskilled workers, as well as critical supply chains.”

China Petroleum Engineering Corp confirmed its involvement in two of the affected sites—a petrochemical processing plant expansion in Fergana and an urban water infrastructure upgrade near Navoi. Company officials in Tashkent expressed “grave concern” over the disruptions, warning of delays and possible long-term repercussions for project delivery. “Our teams are complying with all directives, but we urgently seek clarification and a swift resolution to allow work to resume,” a spokesperson said.

Local analysts estimate that over $1.4 billion of ongoing engineering and construction work has been frozen. “Many of these projects are vital for Uzbekistan’s infrastructure modernization goals,” noted Timur Khamidov, an independent industry analyst. “This blockade is a serious setback both for contractors and for the country’s development timeline.”

The Ministry of Construction issued a brief statement late Wednesday, referring only to “temporary measures” taken in response to “external threats.” No timeline for resumption of work has been given.

Union leaders have called for negotiations to guarantee the safety and job security of affected workers. “We are in talks with government officials to ensure our members are protected during this period of uncertainty,” said Jamila Rakhimova, chair of the Uzbekistan Construction Workers Union.

The situation remains fluid, with further developments expected in the coming days.
